PullRequest.Title: artifacts: Add the shared integration runtime
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

Introduce the provider-neutral runtime for artifact integrations: live resource state, structured details, applicable actions, and explicitly enabled automation.

- Share credential-scoped resource observations while keeping session bindings, trusted origin, consent, checkpoints, and activity separate.
- Centralize configuration revisions, consent generations, durable claims, dispatch fencing, attempt budgets, deduplication, cancellation, and uncertain-outcome reconciliation.
- Provide validated transport contracts, file-backed host persistence, and single-owner browser coordination with Web Locks and IndexedDB.
- Keep presentation data independent of any hover, panel, or provider implementation.

This layer is intentionally infrastructure-only. It does not register a production integration, expose the extension API, or add UI.

## Stack

This is **1 of 4**, based on `main`. Review and merge the stack bottom-up.

| Order | PR | Base |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | **#343002 - Shared integration runtime (this PR)** | `main` |
| 2 | #343001 - Agent host, extension API, and agent tools | #343002 |
| 3 | #343003 - Generic artifact UI | #343001 |
| 4 | #343000 - GitHub pull request integration | #343003 |

The stack replaces the earlier organization in #337678 and #338107; the final layer reconstructs the complete, upstream-integrated feature.

## Validation

Validated this layer independently, without the later layers:

- `npm run compile-client` - **passed**.
- `npm run valid-layers-check` - **passed**.
- `./node_modules/.bin/eslint src/vs/platform/artifactIntegrations --quiet` - **passed**.
- `git diff --cached --check` - **passed** before committing.
- Focused tests below - **85 passed**:

```bash
scripts/test.sh \
  --run src/vs/platform/artifactIntegrations/test/common/artifactIntegrations.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/platform/artifactIntegrations/test/common/artifactIntegrationProtocol.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/platform/artifactIntegrations/test/common/compositeArtifactModel.test.ts \
  --reporter dot
```

No real provider actions or external mutations were executed.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The retention rule and full-ledger transaction path are explicit: each dispatched run in the enabled generation is retained, unique occurrence keys retain at least one run, and every later mutation clones, scans, serializes, and durably rewrites the resulting ledger. Only the real-world occurrence rate is uncertain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Persisted ArtifactRun objects (including prompt/presentation/result payloads), heap copies, JSON bytes, and filesystem operations
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Retained state grows at least linearly with distinct occurrence keys for the entire enabled consent generation, and additionally with every dispatched retry; every transaction then performs work proportional to the enlarged global ledger.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Progressively increasing CPU/GC pressure and durable-write latency, with growing disk usage, for every subsequent run transition or configuration change.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR there was no artifact-integration ledger or durable automation-run history on this path.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new pruning pass exempts every dispatched automation run in the current generation and also the latest run for every occurrence from the nominal 200-run-per-binding history cap.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added RIGHT line 102 calls retained.add(run.id) for every dispatched run in the current enabled generation; added line 104 also retains the latest run for each unique occurrence key.
Findings.Title: Cap current-generation automation history
Findings.Impact: A recurring or event-driven automation left enabled across many occurrences makes action dispatch/completion and configuration changes steadily slower and increasingly I/O-heavy; rich persisted presentations amplify the retained bytes.
Findings.Evidence: pruneSettledRuns first keeps only the last 200 settled runs per binding, but lines 95-107 override that bound for current-generation automation. transact at lines 154-163 deep-clones the entire state, reruns pruning/structural comparison, JSON.stringify's the whole ledger, and writes it. FileArtifactIntegrationStorage performs a temp-file write, file fsync, rename, and directory fsync for each such write. A long-lived enabled automation producing fresh occurrence keys therefore grows both retained bytes and the critical-path cost of every state transition without a bound.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep full ArtifactRun history under the documented per-binding cap. Preserve deduplication and attempt budgets in a compact occurrence index/counter with an explicit lifecycle or quota, retaining full retry chains only while active/indeterminate instead of pinning every run payload for the generation.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: VS Code autorun executes immediately, and the added test explicitly covers an update arriving before the acquire response. The server therefore emits the initial value as an update and returns the same revision/value as the response; the local host forwards these as two separate BroadcastChannel messages.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Serialized snapshot/detail bytes, BroadcastChannel/transport messages, validation work, and temporary objects
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Exactly two full payload transfers occur per artifact or details subscription instead of one; total duplicated bytes scale with opened subscriptions, snapshot richness, detail item count, and receiving windows.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Excess IPC/network traffic and serialization/validation CPU, increasing artifact/details opening cost.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR these artifact subscription payloads and transport messages did not exist.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Installing the new immediate autorun emits revision 1 through onDidUpdate, then request returns the same revision and snapshot; the details branch repeats the same pattern.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added RIGHT line 129 fires the initial artifact snapshot from the immediate autorun, while line 131 returns that same snapshot/revision as the acquire response (and lines 140-142 do likewise for details).
Findings.Title: Send the initial subscription snapshot only once
Findings.Impact: Opening artifact models and expandable details sends and processes every initial full payload twice, multiplied across windows for the local coordinator and across subscriptions in richer views.
Findings.Evidence: ArtifactIntegrationClient subscribes to onDidUpdate before issuing acquire and discards a response whose revision is not newer, so one copy is knowingly redundant. ArtifactIntegrationProtocol.test.ts:95 confirms an update arrives before the acquire response. In LocalArtifactIntegrationHost, endpoint.onDidUpdate sends an update message at line 162 and endpoint.request().then sends a separate response at line 183, proving both payloads cross the BroadcastChannel boundary; artifact snapshots can carry 50 runs and details can carry 200 items.
Findings.Recommendation: Capture the initial observable value for the acquire response without emitting it through onDidUpdate, then begin emitting only subsequent revisions (or suppress the autorun's first callback) for both artifact and details subscriptions.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The pump loops over all runnable ledger entries and schedules each immediately. Both sequencer keys contain the resource identity, so they serialize conflicts but provide no aggregate bound; execute directly reaches authorization, provider preparation/execution, or chat submission. Only the typical burst size is uncertain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Concurrent provider CPU work, network/IPC authorization and chat calls, promises, and cancellation/observation objects
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Aggregate concurrency grows with the number of queued runs whose resource/integration resource keys differ; deduplication and per-key sequencing do not reduce a burst spanning distinct artifacts.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: CPU/network bursts, remote throttling, GC pressure, and reduced interactive throughput when many automations become runnable together.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR there was no shared artifact execution scheduler launching provider actions from a persisted queue.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new pump creates an active token and queues execute for every eligible run in one pass; SequencerByKey only orders runs sharing the same resource-scoped keys.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added RIGHT line 244 queues execute for each run under resourceKey and integrationKey, both of which include per-resource identity, without any shared semaphore or limiter.
Findings.Title: Bound execution across independent resources
Findings.Impact: When automation queues work for many artifacts at once, the host can flood provider/network/chat boundaries and contend with interactive work instead of applying backpressure.
Findings.Evidence: pump iterates the entire run ledger at lines 227-244 and marks every eligible run active. Distinct artifacts have distinct resourceKey and integrationKey values, so their callbacks start concurrently. execute then awaits runtime.authorize, action.prepare and prepared code execution, or runtime.chat.submit, all before the active entry is released. Thus a reconnect/session update or provider event that queues N distinct resources can produce N simultaneous expensive operations.
Findings.Recommendation: Retain the two per-key sequencers for ordering, but place a shared, cancellation-aware concurrency limiter immediately around execute; choose a small bounded parallelism and ensure queued work is removed on revocation/disposal.

Scenarios.Scenario: Creating, dispatching, and completing manual or automated artifact actions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A request first serializes through ArtifactIntegrationStore.transact and a durable full-ledger write; pump then persists preparing/reservation state before provider execution or chat submission. Code actions cross runtime authorization and provider prepare/run; prompt actions cross authorization, detail capture, chat observation, and chat submission. Those boundaries are on the dispatch critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Atomically rewrite and fsync the complete JSON ledger
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full rewrite per non-idempotent transaction; a single action has several state transitions, each serialized through the ledger.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No artifact automation ledger or action-transition writes existed before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Initial creation and dispatch fencing await these writes; later outcome writes delay publication and subsequent sequenced mutations.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Compare-and-swap the complete ledger string in IndexedDB
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One transaction per non-idempotent ledger transition for the browser owner.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No browser artifact ledger existed before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Creation, reservation, and outcome publication await the database transaction.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Authorize and prepare/run provider code actions
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per admitted run after occurrence deduplication; aggregate calls equal runnable distinct artifacts because there is no global limiter.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No shared artifact action scheduler invoked provider actions before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Authorization and preparation must complete before the external effect; run completion must finish before the terminal ledger update.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Observe and submit prompts to the originating/invoking chat
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One observation and at most one submission per admitted run/retry; distinct resources can submit concurrently.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No artifact automation prompt dispatch existed before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Chat availability gates dispatch, and submission acknowledgment gates persisted submitted/running state.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of queued runs after occurrence deduplication, especially distinct artifact/resource keys; number and byte size of retained ledger runs also controls every transition's clone/scan/serialization/write cost.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Resource and integration-resource SequencerByKey lanes serialize conflicting runs only. Both keys are resource-scoped, so N distinct resources can execute N authorize/prepare/run/submit paths concurrently; ledger mutations themselves serialize globally.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Occurrence/request IDs coalesce duplicate submissions and resource pooling coalesces equal canonical resources. These do not coalesce work across distinct artifacts. Warm in-memory ledger access avoids rereading storage but every mutation still rewrites the complete state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the pump starts every eligible distinct key and execute directly reaches provider/chat boundaries; the persistence path and sequencing are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider action cost and typical simultaneous distinct-resource count vary by integration; the unbounded aggregate concurrency and expensive boundary reachability are explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported the unbounded cross-resource concurrency burst. Per-key ordering is sound but does not provide host-wide backpressure.

Scenarios.Scenario: Long-lived enabled automation accumulating occurrence history
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Every run creation, state transition, checkpoint/configuration change clones the full state, runs pruning and structural comparison, serializes the complete ledger, and performs durable storage I/O. The retained history therefore remains directly on all future mutation critical paths.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write, fsync, rename, and directory-fsync the growing full ledger
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One operation per committed mutation; bytes per call grow with all retained runs across bindings.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No persisted artifact run ledger existed before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited by action admission/reservation and configuration/checkpoint operations.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: IndexedDB compare-and-swap of the growing ledger string
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One complete-value CAS per committed mutation; payload grows with retained occurrences.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No local browser ledger existed before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before state publication and dispatch progress.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Deep-clone, compare, and JSON-serialize complete integration state
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per attempted transaction, including idempotent requests up through comparison; input is the complete retained ledger.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No artifact ledger serialization was performed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous CPU/allocation precedes each storage write and result publication.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct occurrence keys in the current enabled consent generation plus every dispatched retry, across bindings; full ArtifactRun payloads can include prompt presentation/details and results.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A global Sequencer serializes transactions, preventing write races but making each enlarged full-ledger operation block all following mutations.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The live state is warm in memory, but pruning exempts current-generation automation runs from the 200-settled-run cap. No compact occurrence index or negative/expiry lifecycle bounds these records.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: retention lines explicitly pin dispatched runs and the latest run for each occurrence; transaction and durable storage costs are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual occurrence frequency and payload richness are provider-dependent, but retention has no upper bound while an option remains enabled and all subsequent transactions consume the full state.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported unbounded retained history because it defeats the advertised per-binding cap and progressively amplifies CPU, GC, disk/database bytes, and mutation latency.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening an artifact or details subscription through the protocol/local browser coordinator
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The client installs an update listener, sends acquire/details, the server acquires the model, immediately emits the current observable value, and then returns the same value as the request response. LocalArtifactIntegrationHost forwards the update and response as distinct BroadcastChannel messages before the client can finish acquisition.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Broadcast initial artifact snapshot as an update and again as a response
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two full messages per artifact subscription rather than one; BroadcastChannel distributes each to all participating windows before target filtering.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No artifact integration protocol messages existed before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both messages are serialized, validated, and delivered during subscription opening; the client discards the non-newer copy.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Broadcast initial details value as an update and again as a response
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two full messages per details subscription; details may contain up to 200 items.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No artifact details protocol existed before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Duplicates transfer and validation work while expandable details are opening.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open/read IndexedDB ledger when becoming the single browser owner
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One database open and authority/state read per owner lifetime, shared across windows by Web Lock.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No local artifact owner/database coordination existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Owner readiness and the first client request wait for initialization; later subscriptions use the warm owner.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of artifact/detail subscriptions, payload size (up to 50 live runs or 200 detail items), and number of open windows receiving BroadcastChannel traffic.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each client endpoint can process requests concurrently; ledger mutations serialize downstream. On reset, client restorers are deliberately serialized with artifacts before details.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Service models and provider details models are reference-counted and shared while leases overlap. Protocol subscriptions themselves are unique, so the duplicate initial message occurs on every cold subscription; reconnect restoration repeats acquisition traffic.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: immediate autorun behavior is exercised by the test for an update arriving before the acquire response, and local host wiring sends update and response separately.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical simultaneous panels/details and snapshot byte sizes vary, but exactly duplicated initial payloads and the cross-boundary path are proven by code and tests.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported duplicate initial payload transfer. Reference sharing avoids duplicate provider models but does not remove the redundant protocol messages.

Scenarios.Scenario: Runtime initialization and restoration of persisted enabled automations
Scenarios.CriticalPath: initialize reads the ledger, then sequentially acquires every distinct retained session/artifact before resolving. Any caller of acquireArtifact awaits initialize, so requested artifact progress waits behind restoration of all earlier retained artifacts. Each model refresh also initializes registered integrations sequentially.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and parse the persisted ledger
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full read per service lifetime.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No artifact ledger startup read existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before restoration or any artifact acquisition.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full read per browser owner lifetime.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No browser artifact ledger startup read existed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire session, match integrations, and create pooled provider resources for retained artifacts
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One model acquisition per distinct retained session/artifact after map deduplication, then one match/create attempt per registered integration not already bound; canonical resource pooling coalesces matching resources.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No artifact automation restoration path existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All retained artifact acquisitions are awaited sequentially before initialize and any acquireArtifact caller can progress.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct retained session/artifact pairs (not raw binding count) multiplied by registered integrations, after canonical resource pooling.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Restored artifacts are serialized by the for/await loop; integrations inside each ArtifactModel.refresh are also serialized. This avoids a startup burst but can sum provider latencies.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: models caches/coalesces a model per session/artifact; ArtifactResourcePool coalesces canonical resources while referenced. Cold startup has no models, while subsequent acquisitions are warm and reference-counted.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the critical-path serialization, lower for expensive provider duration because only asynchronous extension points are present in this layer.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: This PR intentionally ships no production integration, so no concrete network/filesystem behavior or realistic provider latency is available to establish user-visible severity; sequential restoration may also be an intentional correctness/backpressure tradeoff.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding submitted for sequential restoration: the path is structurally scaling, but this infrastructure-only diff does not prove a concrete expensive provider boundary or magnitude. It should be measured once a production integration is wired.

Scenarios.Scenario: Browsing and merging run history across host and client authorities
Scenarios.CriticalPath: CompositeArtifactModel requests an initial page of up to 200 from each active source in parallel, merges by timestamp in memory, and fetches the next page from any exhausted source until it can satisfy the cursor/limit. Remote models turn each page into one protocol history request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one concurrent request per active source per merge iteration; there are currently at most primary and secondary sources, with 200-run source pages.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No composite artifact history protocol existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Requested history cannot return until enough source pages are fetched to locate the cursor and fill the page.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Requested cursor depth and retained runs in the two source models; page size is capped at 200 and output limit at 200.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The two sources fetch in parallel at each iteration; pagination within a source is serial. No unbounded source fan-out exists because the model list is primary plus optional secondary.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: runOwners caches run-to-source routing from invocation/history, but source pages are not cached between getRuns calls. Stored history is nominally capped per binding, apart from the separately reported current-generation retention bypass.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for paging behavior and IPC cardinality.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Deep cursors can reread earlier pages, but practical source count is fixed at two and the diff supplies no evidence of frequent deep-history cancellation/reconciliation requests.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: source fan-out is bounded and parallelized; the material history-scaling problem is the unbounded durable automation retention already reported.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 22 changed files and all diff pages. Submitted three findings: current-generation automation runs defeat history bounds and amplify every durable transaction; independent-resource executions have no shared concurrency limit; and initial artifact/details subscriptions send identical payloads twice. Startup restoration, cache/reference lifecycles, cleanup, history merging, IndexedDB/file boundaries, and local cross-window coordination were also traced without additional high-confidence reportable regressions.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
